_metadata.label: AI-written and not expert-reviewed
_metadata.description: Interview room content for GenAI Engineer track (3 core questions aligned with Neural Mastery criteria, under-20-word spoken follow-ups, robust misconception detectors, and direct Neural Mastery practice links).

dialogue_rules.rule_1_advance_on_excellent: If all points are covered with similarity >= 0.50 and no misconceptions, move on immediately without probing.
dialogue_rules.rule_2_max_two_followups: No question receives more than 2 follow-up probes. Conclude and transition after turn 2.
dialogue_rules.rule_3_misconception_priority: A detected misconception takes precedence on turn 1, phrased conversationally using candidate words.
dialogue_rules.rule_4_single_gap_probe: If points are missed, probe the single most critical unaddressed claim in under 20 words.
dialogue_rules.rule_5_progressive_resolution: If candidate clarifies the probed point on turn 2, acknowledge and advance immediately.

questions.title: What is a foundation model, and how is it different from a regular ML model?
questions.spoken_question: Could you walk me through what a foundation model actually is, and how you think about it differently from a traditional, task-specific ML model?

points.claim: Pretrained at scale on massive, broad datasets to learn general representations rather than trained on narrow, task-specific data.
points.follow_up_spoken: How does the training data and scale differ from training a traditional model?
points.follow_up_template: You mentioned '{phrase}'. How does that training differ from pretraining a foundation model?

wrong_answer_probes.misconception: Defines foundation model strictly as next-token prediction
wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe: Does next-token prediction apply to foundation models in vision or audio?

wrong_answer_probes.misconception: Believes foundation models render traditional ML obsolete for all use cases

wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe_template: You mentioned '{phrase}'. When would you still choose XGBoost over a foundation model?

fundamentals.weak: Defines foundation models purely as ChatGPT or next-token text generation, or claims traditional ML is obsolete.
fundamentals.solid: Defines broad large-scale pretraining, adaptation to multiple tasks, and contrasts with single-task training.
fundamentals.strong: Articulates pretraining representation learning across modalities, explains transfer dynamics, and identifies concrete tabular or latency boundaries.

depth_when_probed.weak: Struggles when probed on non-text models or cannot explain why classical models are still widely used.
depth_when_probed.solid: Clarifies that foundation models include vision and audio representations, and names concrete use cases for classical models.
depth_when_probed.strong: Analyzes pretraining objectives (contrastive, masked, autoregressive), data efficiency of transfer, and serving economics.

trade_offs.weak: Treats foundation models as unconditionally superior with no operational drawbacks.
trade_offs.solid: Compares pretraining vs adaptation costs, serving latency, GPU hardware requirements, and tabular performance.
trade_offs.strong: Evaluates total cost of ownership, cold-start latency, memory constraints, and data governance boundaries.

questions.title: When should you use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) versus fine-tuning, and how do you decide between them?
questions.spoken_question: Suppose an engineering team wants to build an internal assistant over company documentation that updates frequently. How do you evaluate whether to use RAG, fine-tuning, or both?

points.claim: Chooses RAG for dynamic or frequently changing data, and fine-tuning for style, tone, format, or task behavior.
points.follow_up_spoken: How do you decide whether a problem needs new knowledge or new behavior?
points.follow_up_template: You mentioned '{phrase}'. How does that help decide between RAG and fine-tuning?

wrong_answer_probes.misconception: Believes fine-tuning is the standard way to inject new factual knowledge or internal documents
wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe: What happens to fine-tuned weights when tomorrow's documents contradict yesterday's?
wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe_template: You mentioned '{phrase}'. What happens to fine-tuned weights when tomorrow's documents contradict yesterday's?

wrong_answer_probes.misconception: Believes RAG and fine-tuning are mutually exclusive alternatives
wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe: Could you describe a pipeline where you would use both together?
wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe_template: You mentioned '{phrase}'. Could you describe a pipeline where you would use both together?

fundamentals.weak: Suggests fine-tuning to memorize changing documents or treats RAG as merely a low-GPU workaround.
fundamentals.solid: Clearly distinguishes RAG for dynamic knowledge/citations and fine-tuning for format, style, and task behavior.
fundamentals.strong: Delineates parametric vs non-parametric memory and explains when hybrid pipelines are appropriate.

depth_when_probed.weak: Cannot explain how document updates affect model retraining or why fine-tuned models hallucinate citations.
depth_when_probed.solid: Explains catastrophic forgetting, re-indexing operational speed, and citation verification mechanisms.
depth_when_probed.strong: Discusses context length cost curves, precision vs recall in chunk retrieval, and fine-tuning small specialized adapters.

trade_offs.weak: Only mentions GPU cost without considering inference latency, index maintenance, or document ACLs.
trade_offs.solid: Weighs retrieval latency and context token costs against training pipeline maintenance and model drift.
trade_offs.strong: Quantifies break-even request volumes, chunking trade-offs, cache invalidation, and data governance isolation.

questions.title: What is LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation), and why is it preferred over full fine-tuning for production LLMs?
questions.spoken_question: When fine-tuning an LLM for a production task, most teams use LoRA instead of updating all the weights. Could you explain how LoRA works under the hood and why it has become the production default?

points.claim: Freezes the base model weights and trains two small low-rank matrices instead of updating all weights.
points.follow_up_spoken: What is mathematically happening to the base weights during a LoRA forward pass?
points.follow_up_template: You mentioned '{phrase}'. What is happening to the base weights during a LoRA forward pass?

wrong_answer_probes.misconception: Believes LoRA quantizes or compresses the base model weights
wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe: Does standard LoRA quantize weights, or keep them in floating point?
wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe_template: You mentioned '{phrase}'. Does standard LoRA quantize weights, or keep them in floating point?

wrong_answer_probes.misconception: Believes LoRA must remain a separate computational layer during inference that adds latency
wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe: Can the adapter be merged into base weights before serving?
wrong_answer_probes.spoken_probe_template: You mentioned '{phrase}'. Can the adapter be merged into base weights before serving?

fundamentals.weak: Claims LoRA is a quantization method like INT4, or cannot describe what is frozen versus trained.
fundamentals.solid: Explains decomposing Delta W into low-rank matrices B and A, freezing base weights, and cutting trainable parameters.
fundamentals.strong: Formulates the rank decomposition W0 + (alpha/r)*B*A, specifies matrix shapes and initialization, and explains why rank can be small.

depth_when_probed.weak: Does not understand where memory savings come from or thinks inference is always slowed down.
depth_when_probed.solid: Identifies that AdamW optimizer states dominate training VRAM, and explains zero-latency merging.
depth_when_probed.strong: Compares multi-LoRA dynamic batching kernels (S-LoRA/Punica) against weight merging for single-tenant throughput.

trade_offs.weak: Believes LoRA is identical to full fine-tuning with zero trade-offs in expressive power.
trade_offs.solid: Evaluates parameter efficiency vs capacity on extreme domain shifts, and discusses rank selection.
trade_offs.strong: Analyzes memory footprint under concurrent adapter requests, catastrophic forgetting mitigation, and rank selection heuristics.
